items.problem: XAML compiler errors WMC0909 'Cannot resolve DataType', WMC1111 'DataTemplates ... need x:DataType', and WMC9999 internal error were emitted even though the x:DataType and its target type (SDKTemplate.Scenario) were valid; they are a cascade from the failed C# compile. The x:Bind section only lists XLS0414/MC3074 and does not warn about this cascade, risking the agent chasing phantom XAML bugs instead of the real C# error.
items.evidence: migration-score.json winui_build_errors lists WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999 on MainPage.xaml alongside the 4 CS1061; final MainPage.xaml:37-38 has a correct <DataTemplate x:DataType="local:Scenario"> and SampleConfiguration.cs defines public class Scenario in namespace SDKTemplate.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, section '### x:Bind and compiled bindings' (~line 683-685)
items.proposed_improvement: Add one sentence to the existing x:Bind section: WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999 (and other XamlCompiler internal errors) are frequently a *cascade* from a failed C# compile in the same project — resolve all CS errors first, then re-run the build before treating any DataType/x:Bind error as real; do not delete valid x:DataType attributes to chase them.
items.generalizes: The WinUI XamlCompiler runs after C# type resolution and routinely crashes with WMC9999 / mis-reports DataType errors whenever the code-behind or a referenced type failed to compile. Any migration that still has an open C# error (a very common intermediate state) will see these misleading XAML errors, across all scenarios.
